chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).
Regarding a man who raped a woman (of herself), he (peace be upon him) said: He should be killed.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (Imams); refers to either the 5th or 6th Imam.
key_terms.غَصَبَ: To seize or take by force; in this context, to rape.
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: He is killed; indicates the legal ruling of execution.

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a man who rapes a woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from al-Kafi, the Imam establishes that a man who forcibly takes a woman's chastity (ghasaba) is subject to capital punishment, reflecting the severity of violating her bodily autonomy. This verdict underscores the principle of *qisas* (retribution) or judicial execution in Shia jurisprudence for this specific form of forcible intercourse, distinguishing it from other sexual crimes. The brevity of the chain highlights the direct authority of the Imams in deriving legal precedents from the Prophet's tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated either) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>),
regarding a man who raped a woman of herself. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be killed’.
